content:
Before you pay to promote your church's invitation, decide what you want a reader to do. Meta's training starts with a goal, an audience and a budget. Use those decisions to prepare your campaign before opening the advertising controls.

Treat website tracking as a separate decision. Google's advertising policy includes places of worship in a sensitive category, so an ordinary retail retargeting tutorial is not a suitable setup guide for a church campaign.

---

## Choose the response you want

Write a plain description of the response, such as visiting your invitation page. Then select an available advertising objective that fits it. Meta teaches advertisers to align their business goal with an ad objective.

For a website-traffic campaign, Google recommends watching clicks, clickthrough rate, keywords and search terms. Use those measures to evaluate traffic. Keep the campaign's stated goal beside its results when you review it.

<Callout type="important">
Platform guidance checked October 16, 2026. Before spending, confirm current objectives, budget controls, audience restrictions and tracking terms with Meta Blueprint and Google Ads Help. Ask your website provider and counsel which privacy, consent and opt-out rules apply to your church and its visitors.
</Callout>

---

## Choose the advertising tool

A boosted Facebook post is a paid ad made from an existing post. Hootsuite's documentation describes choosing its objective, audience, spend and duration. Meta's own training also covers boosting Facebook and Instagram posts.

| Tool | What you work with |
|---|---|
| Boosted post | An existing post and its promotion settings |
| Meta Ads Manager | Campaign objectives, audiences, placements, creative and reporting |
| Google Search ads | Keywords matched to what people search for |

Use the settings available in your account to compare these approaches. Ads Manager supports creating, managing and tracking campaigns across Facebook, Instagram and Messenger. Google's keyword match types control how closely a keyword must match a search for an ad to enter consideration for the auction.

---

## Prepare the invitation and destination

Check the relationship between the ad and the page it opens. Google considers the usefulness and relevance of both the ad and landing page, along with whether the page meets expectations set by the ad.

For a church invitation, apply that guidance by checking that the destination explains the event advertised. Read the date, meeting place and invitation together before approving the copy. Check that navigation makes the relevant information easy to find.

<Callout type="tip">
Review the destination before paying for traffic. Use Google's landing-page guidance as your check: useful information, relevance to the ad, and easy navigation. Correct a mismatch in the invitation or destination before submitting it.
</Callout>

---

## Set geography, budget and schedule

Google offers location targeting by areas such as cities and by a radius around a location. For a local invitation, review those choices against the area you intend to reach. Check whether the campaign includes people interested in the area as well as people present there.

Google says to consider Presence targeting when you want people in specific locations rather than people elsewhere with an interest in them. Location targeting uses signals and does not guarantee complete accuracy. Review performance after the campaign runs.

Meta Ads Manager lets you set a budget and schedule. Record the chosen settings before publishing. For Google, read the spending rules before approving the amount: an average daily budget can be exceeded on an individual day. Check the applicable spending limits rather than treating that average as a daily ceiling.

---

## Understand retargeting before using it

Retargeting means advertising again to people who previously interacted with you. Google calls its remarketing audiences "your data" segments. Its general documentation describes reaching past website visitors and uploading customer contact information.

Read that description alongside the restrictions. Google identifies personal religious beliefs as a sensitive interest category and lists places of worship among its examples. Advertisers promoting in sensitive categories cannot use advertiser-curated audiences. Google's restricted tools include Customer Match, your data segments and lookalike segments.

<Callout type="warning">
Do not use Google's general remarketing instructions to build a church-visitor or church-contact audience for religious advertising. Its religious-belief policy bars advertiser-curated audiences for that category. Giving someone a consent checkbox does not remove that platform restriction.
</Callout>

Google permits predefined audiences under its sensitive-category rules, subject to the stated restrictions. Review the campaign's actual targeting and landing page with Google support if its status is unclear. Check Meta's current audience and data terms separately before proposing a Meta retargeting campaign.

---

## Review pixels, data and consent

Start with federal guidance. The FTC's business security guide recommends understanding how personal information flows and limiting what you collect. Apply that advice as a practical review of your church's site, with counsel determining the laws that apply.

FTC staff warn that blocking third-party cookies may not entirely prevent tracking pixels from collecting and sharing information. Before enabling Meta Pixel or another advertising tracker, ask your provider what it sends and who receives it. Include the pages and forms it can observe in that review.

Keep the site's privacy explanation consistent with the collection you approve. Ask counsel and your provider to review consent and opt-out needs, then test the choices your site offers. Check the working settings before enabling the tracker.

Google's EU user consent policy, when incorporated into the product agreement, covers end users in the European Economic Area, the UK and Switzerland. It requires legally valid consent for advertising personalization and for cookies or local storage where legally required. Check its full terms if those visitors are involved.

---

## Review before submitting

Use this checklist to apply the goal, creative, audience and spending decisions above:

- [ ] Match the selected objective to the response you want.
- [ ] Read the ad beside its destination page.
- [ ] Confirm geography and any audience restrictions.
- [ ] Check budget type, spending rules and schedule.
- [ ] Review tracking and the site's privacy choices.
- [ ] Identify the report you will use to evaluate results.

For a Google policy restriction, review the ad, destination and targeting. Google's guidance offers correcting the targeting or content, and appealing when you believe the decision is mistaken. Resolve the restriction before treating the campaign as ready.

---

## Review results against the goal

Meta Ads Manager provides campaign metrics for analysis. For a Google traffic campaign, examine clicks and clickthrough rate alongside the keywords and searches that produced them. Use the search-terms report to find relevant searches and identify irrelevant terms to exclude.

Return to your original goal before deciding what to change. Use the results to revise the campaign's settings or keywords. Keep the report and the settings you evaluated together so the next review starts with the same evidence.

<Callout type="scripture">
*"A deceptive balance is an abomination to Yahweh, But a just weight is His delight."* — Proverbs 11:1 (LSB)
</Callout>
excerpt: Choose paid promotion settings, review retargeting restrictions for religious advertising, and check tracking before inviting website traffic.
title: Boosted Posts, Ads and Retargeting

sources.claim: Opening and section 1: goals, audiences and budgets for boosting Facebook and Instagram posts; practical campaign preparation is an application of this training, not a platform mandate.
sources.quote: set clear goals, target your ideal audience, decide on the right budget and optimize ad delivery across various placements

sources.claim: Sections 1, 7 and 8: align the response sought with the chosen objective; keep the goal with the results as a practical application.
sources.quote: define business goals and get started in Meta Ads Manager by selecting an ad objective.

sources.claim: Section 2: boosted Facebook posts are paid ads from existing posts; objective, audience, spending and duration controls are described in the opened Hootsuite guide. No Hootsuite subscription is recommended.
sources.quote: Boosted posts are paid ads that you create from existing Facebook posts. [...] Set your budget and the length of your promotion.

sources.claim: Section 2: Ads Manager creates, manages and tracks campaigns across Facebook, Instagram and Messenger; overview identifies audience, placement, creative and reporting courses.
sources.quote: Meta Ads Manager is your starting point for running ads on Facebook, Instagram and Messenger.

sources.claim: Section 2: Search ads match keywords to search terms; match types control closeness for auction consideration.
sources.quote: Keywords are words or phrases that are used to match ads with the terms people are searching for.

sources.claim: Section 3 and checklist: review relevance, usefulness, expectations and navigation; date, place and event checks apply that guidance to a church invitation.
sources.quote: the usefulness and relevance of your ad and landing page [...] the expectations users have about your landing page [...] ease of landing page navigation

sources.claim: Section 4: available geographic choices, Presence versus Presence or Interest and imperfect accuracy; review choices against the intended area, then evaluate results. No radius minimum or numeric accuracy is asserted.
sources.quote: You only want to target users in specific locations and not users who may be in other locations but are still interested

sources.claim: Section 4 and checklist: Meta budget, schedule and placement settings; recording settings is a practical application.
sources.quote: Learn how to choose placements and set a budget and schedule for ad campaigns in Meta Ads Manager.

sources.claim: Section 4: a Google average daily budget is not an individual-day ceiling; check the spending limits before approving it. No amounts or limit multipliers are given.
sources.quote: on some days you might not reach your average daily budget, and on others you might exceed it.

sources.claim: Section 5: retargeting/re-engagement definition, Google terminology, past website visitors and uploaded contact information. General capabilities are explicitly qualified by the sensitive-category policy.
sources.quote: Use your data to re-engage people who have previously interacted with your brand or services on mobile or desktop.

sources.claim: Opening and section 5: personal religious beliefs are sensitive; places of worship are an example; advertiser-curated audiences are barred. This restriction is not removed by consent. Check the actual ad, destination and targeting or seek support when uncertain.
sources.quote: Content related to personal Religious beliefs is a sensitive interest category. [...] Places of worship [...] You can't use advertiser-curated audiences.

sources.claim: Section 5: prohibited tools include Customer Match, your data segments and lookalike segments; predefined audiences are allowed subject to listed restrictions; general rules do not establish Meta permissions. Section 7: Google gives correction and appeal options.
sources.quote: Customer match [...] Your data segments [...] Lookalike segments [...] Review and remove any advertiser-curated audiences from the targeting settings of your ad.

sources.claim: Section 6: FTC guidance supports mapping information flows, limiting data collection and checking provider sharing. These are recommended practices, not an assertion of universal FTC jurisdiction over churches.
sources.quote: Understanding how personal information moves into, through, and out of your business [...] Keep only what you need for your business.

sources.claim: Section 6: cookie blocking does not necessarily stop pixels; assess data collection and recipients before enabling a tracker. The opened article returned full indexed content once; subsequent requests were intermittently blocked.
sources.quote: Traditional controls such as blocking third party cookies may not entirely prevent pixels from collecting and sharing information.

sources.claim: Section 6: conditional geographic scope of Google consent policy; legally valid consent for personalization and cookie/storage use where legally required. Counsel/provider review is a practical application, not universal consent advice.
sources.quote: incorporates this policy [...] European Economic Area, the UK and Switzerland [...] legally valid consent [...] personalization of ads [...] where legally required

sources.claim: Section 6: consistency with the published privacy article, including review before enabling pixels, asking counsel which rules apply, and testing site choices. Internal source read directly in the worktree.
sources.quote: Ask which privacy, cookie-consent, and opt-out rules apply to your church and its visitors. [...] Keep the notice and the working process in agreement.

sources.claim: Sections 1, 7 and 8: website-traffic metrics, search terms and exclusions; reviewing actual reports against the original traffic goal.
sources.quote: then closely monitor your clicks, CTR, keywords, and search terms.

sources.claim: Section 8 and checklist: Ads Manager metrics support analysis; retaining reports with evaluated settings is a practical recordkeeping application.
sources.quote: Learn where to find key metrics in Meta Ads Manager and how to use them to analyze campaign results.

sources.claim: Closing scripture: Proverbs 11:1 verified individually from the opened verse page. Full verse appears only in the body; excerpt here avoids repeating the complete quotation.

claim_check.notes: Author source mapping complete; independent Opus source, scripture and screenshot review required. No author approval.

rulings: Retargeting scope: Explain mechanics and Google religious-category restrictions before any setup advice. Do not provide a church retargeting recipe, recommend list uploads, or imply consent overrides policy.

Blocked Meta help pages: Use accessible Meta Blueprint pages for confirmed capabilities. Omit claims about Meta sensitive-data terms, exact menu paths, review deadlines, fees, limits and performance promises that could not be checked.

Advice strength and privacy consistency: Campaign worksheets, event checks and report retention are practical applications of cited documentation, not platform or legal mandates. Keep privacy and consent review consistent with the published A14 article. No theology or methodology ruling is proposed.
